findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed liquid eggs stored above butter packets and juice containers. CORRECTED: PIC and staff were notified, and the liquid eggs were moved to the bottom shelf below the ready-to-eat food. Ensure that raw animal products, including raw meat and raw egg products, are stored below RTE foods to prevent contamination from drips from above, as RTE foods are not cooked unlike the raw animal products.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there was an accumulation of debris on the top shelf of the single door cooler next to the walk-in cooler. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. An employee began the process of cleaning the cooler during the inspection. Ensure that the shelving always remains clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the caulking behind the dish sink and the triple sink is missing and/or deteriorating. Both areas are subject to moisture and as such must be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. The base coving (trim) along the wall to the right side of the door to the dish room on the south side of the wall is chipped in the corner leaving the area exposed to moisture and food. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection and a warning notice will be issued to ensure compliance. Ensure that ALL areas subject to food and/or moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection of the facility in 2023. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The both faucets on the left and right side of the triple sink have minor leaks. Equipment and facilities must remain in good repair throughout all operations. Ensure that faucets are repaired/replaced so that they no longer leak.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
A sanitizer bucket was tested for quat sanitizer but read 0 parts per million. Bucket had recently been filled. Operator refilled the bucket and the new sanitizer read at 200 ppm. Corrected on site. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are properly filled and use tests strips to verify concentrations. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The vents in the ceiling of the facility were observed to have a buildup of dust. These vents must be cleaned to protect food from contamination. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.citation_text:
2-401.13 Food employee was observed wearing gloves, but one of their fingers was bandaged and sticking out of the glove. Employee was not using that hand as they normally would because of medical restriction. Employee was advised the bandage still needs to be covered. A larger glove was used to allow the bandage to be covered.
If used, an impermeable cover such as a bandage, finger cot or finger stall located on the wrist, hand or finger of a food employee working with exposed food shall be covered with a single-use glove.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: American cheese slices removed from original packaging did not have a proper date mark. Cheese was opened within the last week and would be used by the following day to prepare meals for students. Date mark was provided. 
Educational handouts on date marking and cheeses exempt from date marking were provided. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C): Food handler certificates were not available for staff. Annual food handler training is completed at the start of every school year. Aramark manager spoke with inspector for options to provide proof of food handler certification for all staff that do not have a CFM (see general comments for details).
Proof of certification needs to be maintained on-site, which can include copies of certifications and/or documentation to verify satisfactory completion of food handler training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Sani-bucket was observed at less than 100ppm quat. Product label states a concentration of 200-400ppm is required for proper sanitization. Solution was made around 8am. Fresh solution was prepared and observed at 200ppm. Chemical absorption into the cloth towels may be part of the reason the concentration was below 200ppm. Consider pre-soaking wiping cloths with sanitizer prior to storage in a fresh solution to help minimize absorption of chemical out of solution into wiping cloths.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: An irreversible registering temperature indicator was not available at the facility for checking the dish machine final rinse surface temperature at the dishes. Options were discussed. Inspector provided some dish machine temperature test strips. Manager will order additional test strips or a plate simulating dishwasher tester for use at the facility. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
The handle to the scoop in the bulk sugar was laying in the sugar.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
The scoop was stored handle up out of the sugar to correct the violation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The wheels on the fryer are soiled with grease and dust.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean the wheels.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Food containers were stored uncovered and food side up on the top shelf in the dry good storage room.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.
The containers were inverted to correct the violation.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
The waste basket in the employees' restroom has no cover.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.
A covered wastebasket was provided to correct the violation.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean

Two tiles are ajar/missing in the dish washing room.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  The tiles were replaced in the grid to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed a build-up of debris in the plastic containers holding measuring cups, etc.  Clean and sanitize the containers.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.
